title: What If You Ate Only Carrots? Your Skin Turns Orange, but Not Your Eyes

scenes.text: What if you ate nothing but carrots? You'd turn orange. But your eyes would stay white.
A carrot holds about five milligrams of beta-carotene. Six or more a day, every day, for weeks, and it builds up.
It's called carotenemia. The pigment settles in your skin's outer layer, thickest on your palms, soles and nose.
Jaundice yellows the whites of your eyes. Carotene never does. That's how doctors tell them apart.
It's most common in babies on carrot or pumpkin purée. First described in 1908. Harmless.
Stop the carrots and the orange fades in weeks to months. Vitamin A overdose from carrots? Virtually never. Your body slows the conversion.

description:
What if you ate only carrots? Beta-carotene would build up in your skin and turn it yellow-orange, a harmless condition called carotenemia.
A medium raw carrot has about 5 mg of beta-carotene; eating more than about 30 mg a day for weeks is enough. The colour shows first on the palms, soles and nose, and unlike jaundice it never tints the whites of the eyes. It is most common in infants fed a lot of carrot, sweet potato or pumpkin purée, and it fades over weeks to months once the diet changes. Carotene from food essentially never causes vitamin A poisoning, because the body limits how much it converts.
